item.title: 照片进去、能推的物体出来：TelePhysica 把「重建」做成会自己找物理参数、还能中途改的闭环 ｜ TelePhysica: Agentic Reconstruction of Physically Interactive Scenes
item.description:
一句话：图生视频把像素合成与隐式潜运动缠在一起，于是没有持久平衡、不能中途干预、也无法反事实施力。

要点：

  • 两条现成路线各自缺一半：**直接的图生视频扩散**把像素合成与隐式潜运动纠缠在一起，因此没有持久的 3D 力学平衡、无法在 rollout 中途干预、也不能施加反事实的力
  • 另一条路线（从未标定照片一次性程序化重建 3D）则把单目深度与支撑间隙留在**欠约束**状态，重建出的场景在重力下会互相穿插或塌掉
  • TelePhysica 的做法是**agentic**：把物理参数与交互性当成需要主动搜索、验证、修正的量，而不是一次前向输出

为什么值得看：「重建出来的东西能不能推」是引擎与仿真的分界。这条把物理可交互性当成要让 agent 去求解的目标（而不是副产物），思路和本周「世界归结构、像素归渲染」的主线一致，但更进一步：连物理参数都要被求解出来。

中文摘要：直接的图生视频扩散模型把像素合成与隐式潜运动纠缠在一起，因此既不保证持久的 3D 力学平衡，也无法在 rollout 中途干预，更做不到反事实的力控制；而「从未标定照片一次性程序化重建 3D」这条路线，会把单目深度与物体与支撑面之间的间隙留在欠约束状态，导致重建场景在重力下互相穿插或直接塌掉。TelePhysica 因此把问题改成 agentic 的：把物理参数、支撑关系与交互性当成需要主动生成、检验与修正的目标，而不是一次前向的副产物。这样重建出的场景不仅几何成立，还能在物理上被推动、被干预。

主题：AI Native Engine

来源：arXiv·cs.CV（English）

原文发布：2026-11-16

本期推送：2026-11-17

Technical Report

TelePhysica: Agentic Reconstruction of Physically Interactive Scenes

Turning Any Visual Content into an Interactive Physical World

Ruiqi Shu*  Xufeng Zhan*  Yuanzhi Liang  Haibin Huang  Chi Zhang  Xuelong Li🖂

Institute of Artificial Intelligence, China Telecom (TeleAI)

††footnotetext: ∗ denotes equal contributions. This work was completed during their internship at TeleAI. Xuelong Li is the corresponding author. ††footnotetext: Homepage: https://interactive4d.vercel.app/

Abstract

Direct image-to-video diffusion models entangle pixel synthesis with implicit latent motion, precluding persistent 3D mechanical equilibrium, mid-rollout intervention, and counterfactual force control. Conversely, single-pass programmatic 3D reconstruction from an uncalibrated photograph leaves monocular depth and support clearance underconstrained, causing reconstructed scenes to interpenetrate or collapse under gravity. We present TelePhysica, a closed-loop framework that reconstructs an executable, multi-regime physical world from a single photograph to drive stateful 3D interaction and trajectory-grounded video synthesis. A vision-language coding agent synthesizes separable visual meshes and declarative physical models within a two-stage verification loop that pairs pixel-aligned silhouette critique with a zero-force gravitational equilibrium preflight. The verified world compiles into a unified solver coupling rigid bodies, articulated chains, co-dimensional cloth shells, and 3D tetrahedral elastodynamics, whose simulated rollouts condition pretrained video diffusion models through pixel-aligned structural streams. On a 100-scene single-image benchmark, closed-loop execution raises equilibrium-verified world recovery from 0% in single-pass synthesis to 81%. Controlled constitutive ablations show over an order-of-magnitude larger localized corner displacement and out-of-plane pleating in finite-element cloth than in matched rigid-plate proxies. Conditioning video diffusion on simulated trajectories increases dynamic motion-mask overlap by 2×--5× and preserves motion direction under counterfactual force reversals where direct image-to-video models fail.

1  Introduction

Predicting how a scene in a single photograph responds to physical interaction—tipping a ceramic mug near its rim, tugging one corner of a bath towel, or indenting an upholstered cushion—requires reasoning over 3D geometry, frictional contact, and material constitutive laws. Sequential and counterfactual interventions further demand an explicit mechanical state rather than a single synthesized clip: reversing a traction vector, shifting a contact point, or applying a mid-rollout impulse alters lever-arm moments, unilateral support reactions, membrane buckling, and volumetric elastic recovery.

Existing generative and inverse-graphics paradigms face two complementary bottlenecks in interactive physical modeling. First, trajectory- and prompt-conditioned video diffusion models inject text cues, 2D strokes, or sparse point tracks directly into latent denoisers [46, 41, 9, 39]. Lacking a persistent 3D mechanical state, these models often freeze deformable surfaces, actuate the wrong object region, or violate momentum balance under counterfactual force reversals. Second, feed-forward 4D synthesis and open-loop inverse-graphics pipelines recover static assets or fixed neural animations [3, 5, 35, 11], while monocular projection leaves depth ordering and support clearance ambiguous along viewing rays. Placed directly under gravity without physical verification, single-pass reconstructions fail through non-manifold geometry, initial collider overlap, or support collapse.

TelePhysica resolves both bottlenecks by decoupling 3D world reconstruction, constitutive dynamics, and photorealistic video synthesis while linking them through executable verification gates (Figure 1). From a single photograph I₀ and scene description p, a vision-language coding agent synthesizes procedural visual meshes and declarative physical models inside a two-stage loop. Stage 1 aligns rendered silhouettes and interior contours with I₀ via pixel-level mask-difference critique; Stage 2 compiles candidate colliders and finite-element meshes into a dynamical solver and enforces a zero-force gravitational equilibrium gate, rejecting floating or interpenetrating layouts that appear valid in 2D projection. Verified worlds then evolve in a unified checkpointable solver spanning rigid bodies, articulated chains, thin-shell cloth, and 3D tetrahedral solids under calibrated surface wrenches, distributed patch tractions, impulses, or prescribed trajectories. Finally, rendered 3D rollouts condition pretrained video generators via structural edge, shaded RGB, or motion-reference streams [38, 14, 1, 29].

Experiments across single-image reconstruction, continuum mechanics, and generative video synthesis establish three principal results:

  • •

    Closed-loop physical world recovery. On a 100-scene single-image benchmark, two-stage verification lifts equilibrium-verified reconstruction from 0% in single-pass open-loop synthesis (2% visual pass) to 81% in a median of 7 scene submissions, while blocking false visual-only acceptance on occluded deformable stacks.

  • •

    Multi-regime constitutive fidelity. Holding geometry, mass, friction, and applied force fixed, co-dimensional finite-element cloth produces >10× larger localized corner travel and 8--11 cm out-of-plane pleating than a matched rigid-plate proxy, while coupled 3D elastodynamics captures sub-millimeter foam rebound and soft-to-rigid momentum transfer.

  • •

    Trajectory-grounded video synthesis. Conditioning video diffusion on simulated 3D rollouts raises dynamic motion-mask intersection-over-union (IoU) from 0.17--0.27 in unconditioned image-to-video baselines to 0.48--0.87, reduces centroid trajectory error by 4×--20×, and maintains >0.90 directional cosine alignment under counterfactual force reversals where unconditioned models yield negative correlation.

    • 2  Related Work

    2.1  Programmatic and Agentic 3D Scene Synthesis

    Representing 3D environments as executable graphics programs provides interpretable hierarchy, separable object instances, and parametric editability. Language-guided layout and procedural modeling systems—including LayoutGPT [7], 3D-GPT [35], SceneCraft [11], and Holodeck [44]—translate text specifications into spatial arrangements or Blender scripts, while BlenderAlchemy [13] and Thinking-in-Blender [10] close a visual render loop to refine materials and geometry. Programmatic world representations also support symbolic physical reasoning in Code-as-Worlds [40] and VisPhyWorld [21], and 4DCodeBench [34] evaluates coding agents on reconstructing observed dynamic trajectories from monocular videos. Complementarily, distributed model cooperation [2, 33] and structure-aware static-scene delivery [47] underscore the efficiency of compact, modular scene abstractions. Rather than fitting a single observed trajectory from multi-frame video, TelePhysica reconstructs an equilibrium-verified physical world from a single static photograph to support diverse post-reconstruction force interventions, mid-rollout continuation, and counterfactual queries.

    2.2  Interactive Physical World Modeling Across Material Regimes

    Coupling 3D scene representations with multi-body and continuum solvers [37, 28, 6] grounds visual synthesis in Newtonian mechanics. Feed-forward 4D generation and score-distillation pipelines [3, 5] synthesize plausible object motion but bake deformation into neural fields without explicit contact colliders. Differentiable continuum twins—including PAC-NeRF [19], PhysGaussian [43], PhysDreamer [50], Spring-Gaus [52], PIE-NeRF [8], PhysMotion [36], and Phys4DGen [24]—embed material-point, spring-mass, or finite-element dynamics into radiance fields or 3D Gaussian splats, generally assuming multi-view captures or isolated foreground objects. For single-view interaction, PhysGen [26] models planar rigid dynamics in image space, whereas PhysGen3D [4], WonderPlay [20], RealWonder [27], PerpetualWonder [48], and Fluid-Gen-Zero [12] lift single photographs into 3D meshes, Gaussian particles, or fluid emitters for action-conditioned rollouts. TelePhysica complements particle-based lifting by compiling agent-synthesized meshes into a unified constraint and finite-element solver that couples six-degree-of-freedom rigid bodies, high-link articulated chains, thin-shell cloth, and 3D tetrahedral solids behind a deterministic checkpoint interface.

    2.3  Trajectory-Conditioned and Aligned Video Generation

    Motion control in video diffusion transformers [45, 15, 38] spans latent trajectory injection and dense structural conditioning. VAST 1.0 [49] decouples storyboard layout planning from pixel generation, whereas DragNUWA [46], MotionCtrl [41], DragAnything [42], Tora [51], Force Prompting [9], and PhysCtrl [39] drive diffusion denoisers with sparse point tracks or local force cues. Without an external 3D contact state, however, out-of-plane rotations, multi-body collisions, and layered cloth disocclusions remain susceptible to silhouette drift and directional ambiguity. Structural video adapters such as VACE [14, 1] inject frame-aligned contour or RGB tensors alongside reference frames, while MiniMax-H3 Ref2VA [29] generates joint audio-video streams from paired appearance and motion references. Orthogonal post-training frameworks align generative trajectories with physical plausibility and spatiotemporal preference rewards [22, 23, 31, 25, 18, 16, 17]. TelePhysica supplies solver-verified 3D rollouts as conditioning streams for pretrained generators and characterizes how model scale and control density govern trajectory fidelity versus material realism.

    3  Method

    TelePhysica maps an input photograph I₀∈ℝ^H×W×3 and scene description p to an executable physical world W₀ and trajectory-grounded video rollouts V̂ through three stages (Figure 1): closed-loop inverse graphics with gravitational equilibrium verification (§3.1), unified multi-regime elastodynamics under calibrated perturbations (§3.2), and deformable surface skinning coupled with structural video diffusion (§3.3). All stages share a right-handed world frame with +Z opposing gravity g=(0,0,-9.81)^⊤ m/s², SI units (m, kg, s, N, Pa), and scalar-first unit quaternions q=(w,x,y,z)∈S³ with rotation matrices R(q)∈SO(3) (Appendix A).

    3.1  Closed-Loop Inverse Graphics and Physical Equilibrium Verification

    Reconstructing an interactive 3D world from an uncalibrated view I₀ requires recovering camera calibration M, separable visual meshes O={oᵢ}ᵢ₌₁^N, collision primitives and finite-element rest topologies ℂ, mobility roles ρᵢ∈{dynamic,kinematic,static,visual-only}, and a statically stable initial mechanical state s₀:

    W₀=(O,ℂ,M,s₀)=A(I₀,p).

    		(1)

    Because perspective projection collapses depth along optical rays, an object floating several centimeters above a tabletop projects to the identical 2D contour as a contacting object when scaled proportionally along its viewing ray. Open-loop single-pass synthesis therefore produces layouts that either misalign in image space or interpenetrate, topple, and drift under gravity.

    To resolve projective and mechanical ambiguity jointly, the reconstruction agent A iterates through a two-stage verification loop inside a headless rendering and physics sandbox. The agent first defines a semantic object inventory with persistent identifiers and mobility roles, keeping movable foreground objects dynamic while locking supporting tables, floors, and walls as static colliders. In Stage 1 (visual mask-difference critique), the agent synthesizes a procedural 3D script specifying manifold visual meshes, physically based materials, lighting, and camera parameters. Rendered per-object silhouettes form an aggregate foreground mask M_rend, which is evaluated against the reference mask M_ref of I₀ via foreground IoU, a 72-bin radial centroid-to-contour profile, and Sobel interior edge overlap. A three-panel diagnostic overlay isolating reference-only deficits and render-only excess guides iterative updates to focal length, object dimensions, and 3D poses.

    Visual alignment alone does not guarantee static support. In Stage 2 (zero-force physical equilibrium preflight), the candidate world compiles into the dynamical solver with zero external actuation (uₜ=0) and integrates under gravity g over T_eq=1.0 s. Acceptance requires bounded initial penetration, scale-calibrated translational or nodal rest, bounded terminal speeds, and numerical solver health across every dynamic object i:

    δ_\max(0)≤ε_c, \max_t∈[0,T_eq]∥xᵢ(t)-xᵢ(0)∥₂≤ε_eq,i, ∥ẋᵢ(T_eq)∥₂≤ε_v,i, finite(sₜ) ∧ N_warn=0,

    		(2)

    alongside rigid-body orientation drift Δθᵢ≤5^∘ and terminal angular speed ∥ωᵢ(T_eq)∥₂≤0.1 rad/s, where δ_\max(0) is maximum initial contact penetration and ε_c, ε_eq,i, and ε_v,i denote feature-scaled tolerances (Table 4). When Stage 2 detects collider overlap, role mismatch, or gravitational drop, structured contact and drift traces feed back to the agent for geometric revision; on multi-body deformable stacks with occluded support clearances, damped quasi-static settling relaxes residual contact gaps before re-verifying Equation (2) so that every exported world W₀ begins at mechanical rest.

    3.2  Unified Multi-Regime Elastodynamics and Surface Perturbations

    Once verified, W₀ maintains an explicit generalized state sₜ=(qₜ,vₜ) independent of any neural video backbone and advances over discrete substeps Δt via sₜ₊₁=S(sₜ,uₜ;W₀). Our declarative schema compiles rigid, articulated, thin-shell, and volumetric deformable objects into a shared contact-coupled formulation [37, 28].

    Multi-Regime Constitutive Formulation.

    Rigid bodies evolve on SE(3) with six velocity coordinates per free body and convex primitive or decomposed colliders subject to elliptic frictional contact cones. Flexible 1D structures such as coiled cables are modeled as capsule chains linked by spherical joints that enforce segment inextensibility while transmitting axial tension and surface friction. Continuum deformables are discretized on a rest finite-element mesh G=(V,𝔼) with nodal positions X(t)=[x₁(t),…,x_V(t)]^⊤∈ℝ^V×3 and lumped masses mₐ>0. In generalized velocity coordinates v, the coupled equations of motion take the form:

    M(q)v̇+c(q,v)+fᵢₙₜ(q,v)=f_grav(q)+J_c(q)^⊤λ_c+fₑₓₜ(t),

    		(3)

    where M(q) combines rigid spatial inertias and deformable nodal masses, c(q,v) collects Coriolis, centrifugal, and gyroscopic bias terms, fᵢₙₜ(q,v) represents passive elastic restoring and viscous damping generalized forces, and J_c(q)^⊤λ_c resolves unilateral normal and Coulomb frictional contacts across rigid-rigid, deformable-rigid, and deformable-deformable pairs via nodal contact spheres of radius r_c. Triangle meshes (|𝔼ₑ|=3, d=2) model woven and knitted textiles through coupled in-plane membrane stretching and cross-edge bending elasticity, complemented by compliant XPBD shell projection in Appendix A. Tetrahedral meshes (|𝔼ₑ|=4, d=3) model compressible foams and cushions via three-dimensional continuum elasticity parameterized by Young’s modulus E>0, Poisson’s ratio ν∈[0,0.5), and viscous damping. Implicit-velocity time integration stabilizes stiff membrane and volumetric modes while coupling deformable contact tractions bidirectionally to dynamic rigid bodies.

    Calibrated Perturbations, State Continuation, and Counterfactuals.

    External actions uₜ enter Equation (3) either as localized surface and material loads or as impulsive and kinematic boundary conditions. For a 2D stroke drawn on I₀ from uₛₜₐᵣₜ to u_end with normalized screen length ℓ=∥u_end-uₛₜₐᵣₜ∥₂, camera ray-casting locates the 3D surface anchor xₐ(t₀) on rigid body oₖ and projects the stroke onto the camera-parallel plane along unit direction d̂∈ℝ³. Weight-proportional scaling with g=9.81 m/s² yields a world-frame force and center-of-mass torque over active window w(t)∈[0,1]:

    F(t)=α ℓ mₖ g w(t) d̂, τ(t)=(xₐ(t)-xₖ(t))×F(t),

    		(4)

    where gain α>0 and lever arm r(t)=xₐ(t)-xₖ(t) generate off-center tipping, pitching, and yawing moments around xₖ(t). On deformable shells and 3D solids, manipulation acts as a distributed material-patch traction F_patch∈ℝ³ over node subset ℙ⊂V with normalized weights ∑_a∈ℙwₐ=1 and smooth \sin² temporal modulation:

    f_ext,a(t)=wₐ F_patch w(t), a∈ℙ, ∑_a∈ℙwₐ=1,

    		(5)

    preventing artificial single-vertex stress singularities. Instantaneous impulses increment generalized velocities via Δv=M(q)⁻¹J_gen at event time t_b, whereas prescribed boundary trajectories drive designated attachment links along quintic smoothstep profiles s(τ)=10τ³-15τ⁴+6τ⁵. Complete solver checkpoints ξₜ serialize generalized coordinates qₜ, velocities vₜ, warm-start contact states, and active perturbation schedules with bit-exact determinism, enabling exact trajectory replay, live mid-rollout continuation at intermediate timestamp t_b, and counterfactual branching from identical initial states s₀.

    3.3  Deformable Surface Skinning and Trajectory-Conditioned Video Diffusion

    To render physics rollouts V_phys=ℝ(s_0:T;W₀) without first-frame pose snapping, each rigid visual mesh preserves its initial body-to-visual offset T_rel,i=T_body,i(0)⁻¹T_vis,i(0)∈SE(3) and updates as T_vis,i(t)=T_body,i(t)T_rel,i. Fine deformable visual meshes resolving hemmed borders, knitted ribs, or upholstery seams beyond the finite-element grid deform via precompiled linear-blend and normal-offset skinning. Each visual vertex pᵣ binds to K simulation nodes {i_r,j}ⱼ₌₁^K with partition-of-unity weights ∑ⱼ₌₁^Kw_r,j=1—spanning direct nodal (K=1), shell barycentric (K=3), and tetrahedral or trilinear cell (K∈{4,8}) bindings—plus a signed thickness offset dᵣ along its carrier triangle (aᵣ,bᵣ,cᵣ):

    pᵣ(t)=∑ⱼ₌₁^Kw_r,j x_i_r,j(t)+dᵣ n̂ᵣ(t), n̂ᵣ(t)=((x_bᵣ(t)-x_aᵣ(t))×(x_cᵣ(t)-x_aᵣ(t)))/(∥(x_bᵣ(t)-x_aᵣ(t))×(x_cᵣ(t)-x_aᵣ(t))∥₂).

    		(6)

    A pretrained video generator G then synthesizes V̂=G(I₀,Φ(V_phys),p_vid) anchored to I₀. Within structural diffusion adapters spanning Wan2.1-VACE 1.3B and Mixture-of-Experts Wan2.2-VACE-Fun A14B [38, 14, 1], we study two pixel-aligned control operators Φ: sparse Canny contours Φ_Canny(V_phys), which constrain silhouettes while leaving interior texture open to reference-guided synthesis, and dense shaded renders Φ_RGB(V_phys), which provide depth-ordered occlusion and surface orientation cues. On rigid scenes, we additionally evaluate dual-reference audio-video synthesis with MiniMax-H3 Ref2VA [29], where Φ_Ref(V_phys)=V_phys, alongside unconditioned direct image-to-video baselines prompted from I₀ without simulated trajectories.

    4  Experiments

    Our experiments evaluate three questions: whether closed-loop equilibrium verification is necessary for single-image 3D world recovery (§4.1), how explicit multi-regime continuum mechanics compares against rigid-body approximations (§4.2), and how simulated 3D rollouts govern trajectory fidelity and appearance preservation in video diffusion (§4.3).

    4.1  Closed-Loop Agentic Reconstruction vs. Single-Pass Open-Loop Synthesis

    We audit complete agent trajectories across our 100-scene single-image tabletop benchmark—covering household vessels, layered stationery, produce, lamps, footwear, and containers—together with three single-image deformable and hybrid reconstructions: a microfiber bath towel, an upholstered seat cushion on a wooden spindle-back chair, and stacked kitchen sponges beside a detergent bottle. Table 1 and Figure 2 compare single-pass open-loop synthesis, evaluated on the agent’s initial scene submission, against full two-stage closed-loop execution.

    On the 100-scene benchmark, single-pass open-loop synthesis passes visual alignment on 2% of inputs and achieves 0% combined visual-and-physical verification. Two sequential failure barriers account for this result (Figure 2b). First, 98 of 100 initial scene scripts fail Stage 1 through non-manifold or misbound procedural meshes (68%), script or renderer exceptions (26%), or silhouette misalignment (4%). Second, after iterative visual critique brings 95 scenes across the Stage-1 visual threshold, 84 of those 95 visually aligned candidates (88.4%) still fail their first Stage-2 physics preflight due to support-plane interpenetration or static/dynamic role errors (45/95), invalid quaternion or inertia specifications (36/95), or gravitational settling drift (3/95). Returning structured execution diagnostics resolves both barriers, recovering 85% visually aligned scenes, 81% equilibrium-verified world packages in a median of 7 scene submissions and 17 tool calls, and 49% verified 5.0 s interactive surface-force rollouts.

    The same two-stage verification governs single-image deformable and hybrid finite-element reconstruction (Figure 2a and Figure 3). Across all three scenes, closed-loop visual critique raises foreground IoU from 0.24--0.37 to 0.52--0.70 (0.60--0.66 composite visual score) with zero initial mesh interpenetration. Both the 121-node bath towel and the 243-node tetrahedral seat cushion satisfy the Stage-2 equilibrium gate autonomously within a single agent run, exhibiting 0.48 mm and 0.98 mm peak nodal drift. On the inclined three-body kitchen sponge stack, Stage 1 reaches clean 2D alignment (IoU 0.55, silhouette structure 0.66) with zero overlap, yet monocular occlusion hides a vertical gap beneath the tilted upper sponge. Stage 2 catches the resulting 68.3 mm peak nodal drop during zero-force preflight to prevent false visual-only acceptance, and damped contact relaxation subsequently establishes full three-body equilibrium (0.66 mm peak nodal drift and ≤0.57 mm CoM drift over 4.0 s).

    4.2  Multi-Regime Stateful Mechanics, Counterfactuals, and Constitutive Ablation

    Figure 4 and Table 2 analyze how constitutive laws govern contact isolation, deformability, and counterfactual interventions across rigid, articulated, thin-shell, and volumetric hybrid worlds.

    Controlled Constitutive Proxy Ablation on Thin-Shell Cloth.

    To test whether thin flexible objects can be approximated by rigid collision proxies, we hold visual geometry, total mass (0.23 kg), tabletop Coulomb friction (μ=0.80), support geometry, and the corner force pulse ([2.6,2.6,0] N over t∈[0.20,0.36] s) fixed on the microfiber bath towel while replacing the 121-node cloth shell with a matched rigid plate (Figure 4a). Enforcing rigid-body kinematics across the 0.76×0.80 m footprint requires overcoming normal friction across the entire sheet simultaneously, limiting motion to a 5.1 cm per-axis (7.2 cm planar norm) slab shift with zero out-of-plane buckling. By contrast, the co-dimensional cloth shell decouples local membrane compliance from distant frictional anchorage: the actuated corner travels more than 10× farther (>52 cm along both tabletop axes, 78.7 cm peak 3D displacement) and buckles into 8--11 cm diagonal pleats while the far corner stays pinned (<0.3 mm motion). Applying the mirrored counterfactual tug ([-2.6,-2.6,0] N) to the opposite corner patch from the same initial state s₀ generates a symmetric fold along the orthogonal diagonal.

    Layered Shell Disocclusion and High-DoF Articulated Tension.

    Explicit contact and joint constraints likewise isolate actuated branches from passive neighbors in multi-body arrangements (Figure 4b–d). On the stacked knitted wool gloves (2×99 shell nodes, with an 831-vertex XPBD shell verification in Appendix A), upward-oblique cuff traction peels the upper glove >38 cm across the lower shell while tabletop friction holds the disoccluded lower glove below 0.7 mm drift. Reversing the traction vector (-F(t)) presses the cuff into unilateral support, suppressing displacement by two orders of magnitude (1.66 mm). Along the 164-segment wired earphone assembly, a prescribed +30 cm lift on the left earbud transmits catenary tension to raise the inline controller and Y-splitter by 9.5--12.2 cm, whereas slack loops beyond the splitter isolate the right earbud (1.3 mm motion). In rigid ensembles, the same checkpointed solver maintains sub-femtometer neighbor isolation across a 2.4 mm pen-holder gap and supports live mid-rollout force or impulse continuation in ten-pin bowling without resetting s₀.

    Volumetric Elastic Recovery and Soft-to-Rigid Momentum Transfer.

    Extending from 2D shells to 3D tetrahedral elastodynamics (d=3) captures through-thickness compression and compliant momentum transfer to movable rigid bodies (Figure 4e–f). Under a downward-oblique load peaking at 32 N vertical force, the 768-tetrahedron seat cushion reaches -5.8 cm peak nodal indentation (-5.1 cm at t=0.90 s) atop a dynamic 4.5 kg wooden chair and recovers elastically upon unloading to within 0.84 mm of its initial height. In the hybrid kitchen sink scene, lateral traction on two stacked 36-node foam sponges (30 g each, E=4.0 kPa) compresses the compliant foam interface against a 0.33 kg rigid detergent bottle and transfers horizontal impulse across the contact patch, sliding the bottle +76.7 mm upright along the wet steel drainboard (μ=0.18) with 0.3 mm X-axis bottle travel sensitivity under Δt/2 refinement.

    4.3  Physics-Grounded Video Synthesis vs. Direct Image-to-Video Generation
